hero.lede: I study how machines come to **feel** — teaching models to infer emotional and cognitive states from physiological signals, and to reason across modalities rather than fire off a single label.

about.heading: A little context
paragraphs: I am a master's student at the **School of Cyber Science and Engineering, Southeast University**. My work sits between **affective computing** and **multimodal learning**: getting a model to read the emotional and cognitive state of a person from signals that were never designed to be read.

Most of my published work is on **cross-subject and cross-dataset EEG emotion recognition**. The hard part is not fitting one person's brainwaves — it is making a model trained on a handful of subjects behave sensibly on someone it has never met, recorded on hardware it has never seen. I approach that with graph-based domain adaptation: align distributions across people and sessions, and let the electrode topology do some of the regularisation for you.

I am currently extending this line toward **multimodal reasoning**, where language, vision and physiological streams are used jointly to infer affect and intent instead of collapsing everything into one label.

research.heading: What I work on
research.sub: Two directions I keep coming back to — reading affect from signals that were never designed to be read, and reasoning across modalities about why a state holds.

items.title: Multimodal Reasoning
items.text: Joint inference over language, vision and physiology. Rather than a single fused classifier, I am interested in models that reason about *why* a state holds and can be asked follow-up questions about it.

items.title: Affective Computing
items.text: Estimating emotional and cognitive states from physiological signals — EEG first, with peripheral signals as a complement. The goal is a reading that is stable enough to trust outside the lab.
Two papers accepted to **IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing** — on multi-scale temporal modelling and cross-dataset graph alignment.
*MLDA-STG* and *EmoVAE* appear at the **Annual Meeting of the Cognitive Science Society**.
Paper on multi-dimensional feature fusion and multi-level domain adaptation accepted to **ICASSP 2026**.
*PR-DA* accepted to **IEEE BIBM 2025**; code released on GitHub.
Paper on progressive multi-domain adaptation published in **IEEE TNSRE** — with code.
